item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is substantially closer to the frozen contract because it limits the change to Files.Upload and its tests. B makes an explicitly prohibited global retry/body-buffering change that alters Files.Add and every other RawClient reader request.","reasons":["Both patches incorrectly duplicate FilesService.Add internals instead of routing Upload through Add, but A avoids B's much broader contract violation.","B changes RawClient.Do to eagerly consume arbitrary io.Reader bodies whenever retries are not explicitly disabled, altering request timing, memory use, reader-error behavior, and streaming semantics across the SDK.","B explicitly changes Files.Add behavior and advertises that change, conflicting with the requirement to preserve Add's existing behavior and avoid refactoring unrelated retry machinery.","A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and produces a replayable multipart body while preserving FilesOption propagation and response/error handling semantics in equivalent code."],"risks_a":["Upload does not call FilesService.Add as required, leaving duplicated request construction and response decoding.","It lacks the required source-reader failure test.","Its retry test starts with a bytes.Reader rather than an opaque streamed source, so it does not directly demonstrate streamed-content handling by NewFile—although it verifies the generated multipart body is resent intact on retry."],"risks_b":["Upload also bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its implementation.","The RawClient change violates scope and can unexpectedly buffer very large bodies throughout the SDK.","It changes Files.Add semantics despite the explicit preservation requirement, and also affects Update and unrelated endpoints using RawClient.Do with readers automatically initiating reads before any request is made and retries independent of whether a method is retry-eligible under policy other than WithNoRetry()."]}
